messages:
Ellen: NeoHealth POC: they asked for Private/VPC connectivity options + a short cost note. Key asks: preserve client source IP for audit logs, support for TLS-inspect in their egress stack, and firewall allowlist for the POC. Also want any one-time setup fees called out.
Victor: Network summary for them:
- VPC Peering: preserves client source IP. Requires route table updates, possible account limits, and peering connection acceptance in both accounts. Good for full L3 access.
- AWS PrivateLink (Interface Endpoint): exposes service as ENIs in their VPC. Simpler security posture, minimal routing changes, but original public client IP is not visible to our backend by default. We can accept X-Forwarded-For headers if the client's edge forwards them.
Sam: NeoHealth says their SIEM ingests raw client IPs for compliance. That makes plain PrivateLink risky unless they can add X-Forwarded-For.
Maya: Mitigations/options:
1) Recommend VPC peering for the POC to satisfy logging requirement.
2) If they can't peer, propose a lightweight forward proxy in their VPC (we can supply an AMI or container) that forwards original client IP via XFF; Redwood Private can consume XFF for logs.
3) Offer an in-VPC Redwood Private short-term deployment (customer-managed) so traffic originates from their subnet and client IPs are preserved.
Omar: TLS inspection: if their egress appliance does MITM, it will break certificate pinning and SNI. Recommended approach: allowlist our service domain/IPs on their TLS-inspectors to bypass MITM. If they insist on inspect+cannot bypass, discuss mTLS or client certs as an option but that increases setup time and may be out-of-scope for rapid POC.
Victor: Firewall snippet we usually provide:
```
# Example allowlist for NeoHealth POC
Allow TCP 443 -> 34.199.88.101/32  # redwood-poc-1
Allow TCP 443 -> 34.199.88.102/32  # redwood-poc-2
Allow UDP 53   -> <their-dns-resolver-ip>
# If using PrivateLink, allow TCP 443 to the interface endpoint ENI IPs instead of public IPs above.
```
Ellen: Pricing note: for a two-week POC we typically waive platform fees and cover small ephemeral infra; if they request static EIP, dedicated NAT, or BYOIP, we add a one-time provisioning fee + ongoing infra costs in the SOW. I'll flag with finance for a quick estimate.
Maya: Some customers worry about MTU fragmentation with PrivateLink and proxy hops; recommend leaving PMTU enabled and test with representative payload sizes.
NetBot: Created ephemeral preview endpoint: https://preview-1716667777.redwood.test (expires 14 days).
Sam: Action items: Victor draft 1-page peering vs PrivateLink diagram + include proxy pattern. Ellen coordinate finance estimate for BYOIP/static eip. Maya draft brief TLS-inspect guidance. I'll share with NeoHealth NW contact and propose a short call to decide peering vs PrivateLink.
Ellen: Thanks all, will follow up after the call. :thumbsup:
